verdict: A near-identical rebuild of the Community feed whose main gaps are the featured photo scaled about 5% larger and a few text details (heavier, larger EN label, a different extract truncation, slightly tighter Roboto spacing); a clean flex structure with a templated bottom navigation.

top_defects.what: badge photo is scaled about 5% larger and sits a few px lower: the crown and the frame edges are offset and the grey margin on the right of the badge is gone. The grid cells over the image reach a meanDiff of 24 to 39

the card is set to h-[444px] with object-cover rather than matching the reference's crop of the photo, so the whole image region drifts. Smaller offsets: the tab labels sit about 1 px high and the language button is 1 to 2 px off
the label is 12px medium and fills the dark box, where the reference uses a smaller, lighter label (about 10 to 11 dp regular) with visible padding

top_defects.where: banner text, module description, article extract
top_defects.what: the Roboto glyph spacing is slightly tighter than the reference, so the words drift a few px along each line (they show doubled in the heatmap). The extract uses tracking-[-0.35px] at 15px instead of matching the reference's metrics
the line ends "Cheltenham…"; the reference cuts mid-word with "Cheltenham Tr…"
the Wi-Fi and battery glyphs are about 10% larger and heavier than the reference's
136 arbitrary values and no shared tokens: #202122, #54595d and #3366cc are repeated literals. The two round action buttons and the tabs are copy-pasted; only the bottom navigation is a template

strengths: Every element and text of the reference is present with the measured colors (#202122, #54595d, #3366cc, #eaecf0, #e8f0ff, #b32424), including the red "new" dots and the 39% black overlay on the photo
The bottom navigation is one data-driven template (5 items) with per-item pill, badge and label classes, and it matches the reference closely
Header, banner, section header and card are flex groups with readable names; the text is real text, and the icons are the app's own SVG assets
